check.name: lens.conventions
check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

snippet.text: | `probe` | `read`, a list of paths relative to the checkout that a probe reads beyond the head's tracked tree: `node_modules` links the dependency install in, and any other path is copied in. `Probe` refuses an absolute path, a `..` segment, the checkout itself and a path that resolves outside it, and refuses the probe when the copies together pass 50,000 entries, 512 MiB or 60 seconds, or meet anything but a file, directory or link. The deadline is read before and after each entry on a monotonic clock, so a copy runs at most one entry past it. Only a committed root `melian.yaml` sets it, read from the base. Nested policy and preference files are refused | `read: [node_modules]` |

message.text: The change adds the `melian.yaml` key `probe.conditions` to `melianYamlSchema`, `MelianConfig` and `defaultConfig`, but the key table's `probe` row in docs/guidelines/core.md still lists only `read` with default `read: [node_modules]`.

explanation.what: The change adds the `melian.yaml` key `probe.conditions` to `melianYamlSchema`, `MelianConfig` and `defaultConfig`, but the key table's `probe` row in docs/guidelines/core.md still lists only `read` with default `read: [node_modules]`.
explanation.whatToDo: Add `conditions` to the `probe` row: at most 16 Node conditions of at most 100 characters matching `probeConditions.pattern`, root-only, read from the base, default `[]`.
explanation.whyHere: packages/core/AGENTS.md: "A new `melian.yaml` key goes into `melianYamlSchema`, `MelianConfig`, `defaultConfig`, and the key table in the guideline together." AGENTS.md also says "Update documentation in the same change whenever behaviour diverges from what is documented."

properties.failureScenario: A contributor reads the core guideline's key table to configure probes, finds only `probe.read`, and never learns that `probe.conditions` exists or its limits. The table states a default of `read: [node_modules]` while `defaultConfig.probe` is now `{ read: ["node_modules"], conditions: [] }`.

snippet.text: | `melian doctor` | Checks Node, git and `--attr-source`, Pi's login, providers with credentials, the GitHub token's source, gh, and the repository. It names which `melian` ran and warns when it lies inside the checkout. The `clone` line names the linked git clone, its commit, and whether its tree is clean. It warns when the clone is dirty or git cannot read it. An install under `node_modules` omits that line. Doctor also checks the state directory and whether it is writable. Its `evidence` line names the evidence directory, its size and `evidence.budget`, and warns once the directory has reached the budget, since a valid miss then keeps no more until `evidence.budget` is raised in the configuration; `melian store prune` keeps evidence until [issue #633](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/633) lands. Its `records` line, when the checkout has an `origin`, fetches the `melian/state` branch's tip into the store's own repository. It names, as a warning, up to five files on it that Melian did not write, which refuse calls until a writer removes them, or warns that the branch cannot be read. Opening the store sweeps what killed calls left in the state directory, and the line warns about what that sweep left: up to five leftovers it kept because it cannot tell their maker is gone, up to five of an exited call it could not remove, how many stale ones it ran out of time to remove, or left because it could not list every leftover, which the next open removes, that it stopped listing at its bound of 1,000 leftovers, and a process table it could not read, which sweeps nothing and keeps every leftover it found. It names them after the branch's own warning when the branch cannot be read, since the sweep ran when the store opened. A sweep that removed all it found says nothing. The same line then says whom the committed root policy trusts to write the branch. It reads `trust.writers` from the same base as the `trust` line. With it on, the line says the branch's writers are trusted as the repository's w [cut at 2 KiB]

message.text: `melian doctor`'s `probes` line now also runs a probe that runs `git init` and warns when git cannot run in a probe. The CLI guideline's doctor row still says the line "runs an empty probe and says whether probes run here, or why every probe is refused, as a warning".

explanation.what: `melian doctor`'s `probes` line now also runs a probe that runs `git init` and warns when git cannot run in a probe. The CLI guideline's doctor row still says the line "runs an empty probe and says whether probes run here, or why every probe is refused, as a warning".
explanation.whatToDo: Amend the doctor row to say the `probes` line also runs a probe that runs `git init`, prints `git included` when it runs, and warns with git's reason when it does not.
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md: "Update documentation in the same change whenever behaviour diverges from what is documented." The change updated design.md but left the CLI guideline's command table alone.

properties.failureScenario: On macOS with no developer tools, doctor prints `warn probes run under sandbox-runtime, but git cannot run in one, ...`. A reader of cli.md expects a warning only when every probe is refused, so they read this warning as probes being refused.
